messages.content: Alonsa wakes at the start of a new day. The sun is rising, the smell of burning ash is palpable in the air, and the sound of wind rushing past would knock her off her feet were she not laying down. Suddenly, something flies overhead. Tens of meters long, colored a crimson red, and covered in scales. A dragon has arrived, breathing fire from its maw.
"What?"
"Is this..."
"Am I still in the dream?
A figure runs past. "What are you doing!? You got a death wish? Run!" It's hard to make out their features from the ground, but their voice is unfamiliar.
Alonsa starts running with the person, whoever they are.

As she runs alongside them, the person turns to Alonsa. A straight blade is gripped within their palms, and plate armor covers their body. "Hark, traveler! What brings you to such a dangerous place? Forgive me, but you do not seem like a warrior."
Her voice falters off.
She examines her surroundings. Where is she?

There's... something familiar about her surroundings, but it doesn't quite look like anywhere she's been before. There are rolling hills covered in lush greenery. In the distance is a town of an older era, built with primitive techniques, and in the other direction is what appears to be a vast forest, filled with colorful flora she's never seen before.
"Where am I?"
"Am I awake?"
"What's going on..."

"This is no dream. You've found yourself in the land of Paradise. Not sure how you made it through the Dark Forest, if you didn't even know where you were going." As the knight speaks, the dragon suddenly dives downward above them, landing with the thunderous crash in front of them. It rears its head back, ready to attack.
"Paradise?"
Alonsa is thrown back suddenly by the dragon.
"What... is that a dragon?"
"They don't... they can't... they're extinct..."

"You appear confused traveler..." The knight grips the sword tightly in their hands. "...But this is no time for explanations. This blasted beast is a scourge upon this land. I am afraid this may be our end, but I will not go down without a fight, for that is my vow!"
*Is this a dream? It feels too real... I can feel that thing shaking the ground when it moves.*
She braces herself for the dragon's attack.

Fire erupts from the dragon's mouth, rushing towards her and the knight. All of a sudden, it appears to hit an invisible wall in front of her. It rushes around her body, but never touching her, as if there were a sphere protecting her.
"Huh?"
It's not even hot...
"What's going on???"
"Mr. Knight?"

The knight chuckles. "The cavalry has arrived, it would appear." They motion to three figures rushing towards the dragon from behind.

The first, a woman in carrying a lute, strums a song as she runs. "Protect, protect, protect 🎶 Our newfound friend 🎶 Reflect, reflect, reflect 🎶 A fiery, painful end 🎶"

The second, a woman in robes, extends her hands towards the dragon. "Lightning." She speaks with confidence as a bolt of electricity erupts from her palms towards the dragon, causing it to cry out in pain.

The third, in what appears to be religious attire, rushes to the side of the knight. "Cure wounds!" They yell out, as the knight's burns, on the segments of exposed skin in the gaps of their armor, appear to disappear entirely.
*What is this magic... This is far more powerful then any magic I can remember...*

"My comrades... I thank you. Without your aid, I would be unable to fell this foul beast. Now, with the blessing the Hero's Guild, I shall smite you from this hallowed ground!" The knight leaps forward, and with a single swing of their sword, cleaves the dragon's neck in two. Its head falls to the ground in front of Alonsa, the light draining from its eyes.

Alonsa approaches the dragon's head, and studies it. Lizard-like scales, but cat-like eyes. Horns made of bone, like a goats. Massive, protruding teeth. This kind of creature... It's not possible. It can't exist.
And yet it does. Right before her.
"Where's Tanner? And Atie, where's Atie?"
"This must be some... Theo must have done this. Him messing with the casts, it must have thrown me into this... whatever this place is."

The knight places his foot upon the dragon's head, displaying their victory over it. "Traveler, I know not of this Theo, nor of this Atie, but I met Sir Tanner this morn. I can take you to him, if you wish." They sheathe their sword. "But first, allow me to introduce you to my adventuring party. Were we not in mortal danger 'til this very moment, I would consider it quite rude that I have failed to do so."
*Of course, out of everyone to follow me into this new world, it's Tanner.*
"Sure! I didn't get a chance to introduce myself before. I'm Alonsa."

"Greetings, Alonsa! It is a pleasure to make your acquaintance." The knight motions to the bard, currently playing a celebratory song of victory. "This is Bushy Stevens. She is an aspiring musician from the North, and a reliable ally on our quest for justice." Then the wizard in robes, standing stoically to the side. "Frompt Sneevs, the wisest scholar I have ever met. A boundless font of knowledge on the arcane." Then the Cleric, hands clasped in prayer. "Shorts Kildoc, a fastidious practitioner, and an ally to all in need." And finally, they remove their helmet, revealing a feminine face. "I am Sir Roost, of the Hero's Guild. I have come here to bring an end to the pointless conflict of this region."

With them all lined up, and Roost's face revealed, something clicks in Alonsa's head. Somehow, in some way, the shapes of this group are familiar. Very familiar. Stevens to Briar. Sneevs to Penny. Roost to Bucky. Finally, Kildoc has the same exact shape as Alonsa herself.
"Nice to meet you..."
Shes choosing not to think about the shapes thing.
"You said that we're in Paradise?"

"Indeed! The land of wishes, where dreams come true, and magic is at its strongest. Tales say that the font of magic's origin sprouted from that very hamlet." He motions to the village in the distance. "For many years, it knew a peace like no other. But now, it is under threat from the East and West at once. Two armies are set to converge here, both seeking the source of magic. There are even rumors that the Great Demon Lord intends to send his army in the fray as well."
“Demon Lord?”
“Wait, who are these… people in the east and west? They wouldn’t happen to be Newark and Yondova, would they?”

"I'm unfamiliar with those names, I'm afraid. You speak of many strange things, traveler. To the East is the army of Kham, from the sweltering land of sands. To the west is the army of Muk, from the frigid land of crows." These are the names of civilizations known to exist, but too old for much to be known of them in historical records. Sir Roost's hand curls into a fist. "The Demon Lord hails from neither. Some say he comes from beyond Turtima itself, from the realm of demons. He brings naught but misery and suffering when he descends upon a region."
"Turtima. That's the continent we're on?"
"Of course it is, where else is there..."
"I think I know what's going on, Sir Roost. Before I tell you, I have to talk with Tanner."

"Very well. I am interested in your tale, Alonsa." He claps to get his party's attention. "I shall accompany this traveler into town. The rest of you, return to camp, and prepare for battle." The others acquiesce, and set off towards the forest. Roost turns back to Alonsa. "Shall we, then?"
She nods at him, and walks alongside.
He holds his helmet in one hand as he leads the way into town. "How are you familiar with Sir Tanner? He is... quite the character, to say the least. Our meeting is not one I am soon to forget."
"Where I come from, he's my... employer."
"I imagine he has a lot of thoughts about what's happening."
Alonsa pulls out her notebook.
"Speaking of which, I do have a few questions."
He nods. "Go ahead, I will be happy to provide any answers I am capable of."

"Where do you come from? And the rest of your group, where do they come from? What metal is your armor made of, and how did you get it? Where exactly did your wizard learn their spells? What religion does Shorts practice? From where did it come from? What is the history of the two kingdoms? Why..." She has to pause, as she's out of breath, from speaking so quickly.

"Hah! Very curious, aren't you? Do you intend to novelize our adventures?" He shakes head. "I come from the west, a small town outside of Muk, known as Joonk. I picked up the rest of my party on my travels from there to Paradise. My armor was provided by the Hero's Guild, upon my rising to the rank of Paladin. I cannot say I am aware of what it is forged from, but it magically blessed, as is my blade. Ah, what was the next one...?"
"The magic! That was another one. Where I come from, magic is a lot... smaller. Even the most skilled mages can't do the things you guys do casually. How are you doing this?"
He shrugs. "I'm afraid I cannot say why your land is so... ah, magically inept? Perhaps magic's decay was simply expediated in that region?"
*Don't like the implications of that!*
"It's no matter. Anyway, the kingdoms. Where did they come from?"
"Why are they fighting?"

"They rose as any other kingdoms did. Bloody conflicts, hostile takeovers, and political schemes. Each has a long and storied history, but they are likely the two most powerful nations on the face of Turtima. In terms of military strength, at least." His voice turns ever so slightly more grave. "They fight to find the font of magic that blessed this world in times untold. Once, the people were thankful for their gifts, their powerful abilities. Ever since its decay was discovered, however... both kingdoms realized that eventually their greatest asset, their magical power, will disappear. Whoever can reach the source of magic may be able to harness the great forces only seen in legends."
"Which legends?"
"The Prince? The Reaper?

"I'm afraid I'm not familiar with those. I meant the legends of Turtima's creation. When the old masters of magic shaped its very land, harnessing the forces of nature." The two of them arrive in the town as they speak. It's about the same size as the Paradise in which Alonsa is familiar with, but notably lacking a visible church, or a mansion on the other end.
*Of course there's no church... They haven't built it yet.*
*Bell, the religion the church is based on hasn't even happened yet.*
"What do you mean by old masters?"
"Where did they come from?'

"It is said that they were born from the primordial sea of glass, granted thought by the arrival of magic, and given form through their own will. They shaped Turtima to house the arrival of life, born from magic, spreading out from this very town as its center."
"What happened to them?"

"Hah, well, they certainly don't seem to be around today. Sorry, you'd have to ask Frompt. I'm no scholar, I just hear things." They stop in front of an inn. It's not the Narita Inn, the construction is entirely different, but it's in more or less the same location. "Sir Tanner is staying here, I believe."
"Thank you! I might come back with more questions later. And thanks for saving me!"
"Of course! It is my solemn vow to defend all from evil. Stay safe, and good luck, Alonsa the curious traveler!" He departs in the direction they entered town from.
Alonsa heads into the Inn, and searches for Tanner

She finds him in the lobby, but he doesn't seem to notice her enter. His hair is a mess, and he appears frenzied. He scribbles furiously on sheets of parchment, occasionally stopping to nervously chew on the quill he's writing with.
"Tanner?"

His shoulders shoot up, and his head snaps towards her. He seems to relax a little when he processes who spoke to him. "Alonsa... I... I wasn't sure if you'd... be here... I didn't know if... if that memory was just..."
"I thought this was a dream at first too."
She sits next to him.
"What happened?"
"...Do you... do you remember? What the world was like? What... what it was like before this?" His eyes are begging her to remember.
"Of course I do!"
"I was... We were just there!"
"And... this isn't a different world, Tanner. The world hasn't changed, we're the ones who've changed. We've been cast into the past. We're in history!"

"Is... Is that so... So we were in the future..." He places his head in his hands. His voice is strained, as if pushing himself to the limit. "I'm asking, Alonsa, because... I *can't* remember. I know this isn't right. Obviously. How could this be the world... or... the time I was born in. But I have these memories... as if I've been here my whole life... and as if you have too. What happened to me...?"
((End session))
Alonsa pauses
She tries to remember if she had her own set of memories in this world, too.
Alonsa doesn't remember ever having been in a world or time that resembles her surroundings before today.
“I’m sorry, I… I remember it, as well. Do you not remember? We spent a lot of time together. What about your sister?”

"I... I haven't seen her today... Were we sent to different times...? I remember being with you last night... are we together due to proximity?" He shakes his head. "No, I can't believe that. She would be lost to me, if that were true."
“She wasn’t with us when… whatever happened hit.”
“I don’t know what could’ve caused this, but…”
“This is just a hunch, but I think it was probably localized to the church. So it’s just you, me and Atie.”
“Plus whoever else was inside.”
“Your sister is probably still at the train.”

"So, we just need to find a way back..." He leans back in his chair, still keeping a hand on his head. "...Problem is, I don't remember a church. I knew we were together, just not... where. If my memories were... refitted, to match this time, then the church must not have been built yet."
“Do you remember… me?”
“Better question: do I exist in your memory of this world?”

"Yes, but... if I'm right, it's just... my false and true memories overlapping. Any memories I have from the future, or... our present, I suppose... the ones that weren't too contradictory must have been altered. To fit my new life story."
“What’s different about the new one and the old one?”

"I don't... Agh!" He almost looks like he's in physical pain trying to remember. "I just... can *feel* that my new memories are wrong. The things you were studying, that I was studying... where we worked and lived... it doesn't click. It's sloppily put together, but... it's still all I remember. My history *here*, in *this* time, and any true memories that could fit in it. Any that couldn't were... discarded. So, I couldn't tell you what my old memories were like."
“I’m sorry. I don’t want to push you.”
“Listen… you knew much more about the casts then I did.”
“Do you think Theo could’ve done something that would’ve… brought us here?”

"It's... not something I fully understand, but... this still feels like too much. I can't think of anything about the casts that could move us through time. It doesn't make sense. Either this is unrelated, or I truly understood nothing."
“You said that they could alter reality, right?”
“Or… change memories, or something.”
“Maybe this is an extended version of that.”

"It... would explain how my memories were changed, yes. One would merely need to reshape my brain while I'm within a cast. Still, I don't see how we'd actually be able to *get* to the past. Unless... it's our perception of the world that was altered? Perhaps we only *think* we're in the past..."
“That…”
“That seems impossible.”
“Then… what’s really going on? Where are we?”
“Are we still in the church?”
“No, because… I was outside of town..”
“Ugh, whatever.”
“No, I don’t think…. If this is all a hallucination, I can’t imagine it would be shared.”
She picks up a cup from the table. “What color is this.” To her, the cup is brown
"Brown."
“Yeah! See!”
“So… it’s a shared reality, of some kind.”
“Or like… we’re experiencing the same things. Which means this can’t be an illusion.”
Unless, of course, Tanner being here is part of the illusion. But she’s not gonna worry about that now.

"That... makes sense. It would be improbable for our brains to fill in the gaps in the same way." He pauses, staring at the cup. After a moment, he softly laughs. "You know, this is all a bit ironic, in a way."
“How so?”

"...I always talked about the future, didn't I? That must still be the same, surely. You were always so concerned with learning the secrets of the past, just... just for the sake of it, really." This is the first thing he's seemed to enjoy talking about since this conversation began. "I... I just couldn't do that. I wanted to change the future, create a better one. But that was settling, it always was. What I wanted, what I really wanted, was to change the past. It's... an impossible dream, but I had to hold onto it. I had to."
“…If we really did get transported back in time somehow, you might have just been given the chance to.”
“But I’ve never wanted that, I’m sorry. The mistakes of the past… as bad as they are, we need to be able to learn from them. Otherwise, we’ll make the same mistakes.”
“And we’ll become the past that others learn from.”
She thinks “Memories are, in a lot of ways, all we have.” But she doesn’t say it. She doesn’t want to tell him that he’s got nothing.

"...Hah. Yeah, that's right, isn't it. That's why everything turned out like this. I couldn't look back. It... it scared me, the thought of accepting how things were. So I never learned, did I?" He shakes his head. "Aw hell, I need a drink."
“What’s past is past. Now you’ve got another chance to learn from it.”
She sits down next to him.
“What do we even do now? Look for the others, who might have come here, I guess.”
"Right. We can likely assume Theo and Ms. Alcule will be here. Who else would've been in that church? Hopefully I haven't... forgotten any faces, or names."
“I don’t know…”
“Briar? Bucky, maybe?”
“I haven’t seen them in a while.”
“Who else might have been working with Theo?”
“That’s honestly what doesn’t make sense to me… why is he doing this?”

"...Theo McGregor is a brilliant man. I've only spent a short time with him, but he's a master at using what he has at his disposal to reach his ambitions. He wasn't just the... um..." He snaps his fingers, trying to remember. "...head of... what we used to get here. He discovered the inventor of it himself, then marketed it and brought it before the prime minister. When I told him of the casts, he saw an opportunity. The chance to make his dreams a reality. What they were specifically, he didn't say, but... if I had to guess, I'd say this is all for his sister."
“That… that seems likely, yeah.”
“Then I’m guessing, she’s also here, isn’t she?”
“But why… what did the emperor have to do with any of this?”

"..." He strokes his chin. "Perhaps he wished to rid himself of competition? If the emperor knew anything about the casts, or if Theo even suspected he did... then he would certainly have the resources to outman Theo, and it's unlikely their goals would align."
“Do you think that’s what the emperor wanted?”
Alonsa suddenly remembers the conversation she had with one of the emperors guards.
“They did promise to tear this place down.”
“Or… that place, I guess.”

"I suppose Theo wasn't too far off the mark, then. Personally, I only met the emperor in passing. I don't really know enough about the guy, especially now that I can't even remember what nation he ruled."
“Hehehe…”
“To tell you the truth, Tanner. I remember about as much about it as you do, and I still remember everything.”
“I didn’t even recognize him as the emperor when I saw him. I’m really out of touch, aren’t I.”
“Whatever…”
“I guess it’s in the past.”
"Well, it'd be in the future, but who's keeping track." He smirks for a brief moment. "Shall we get searching, then?"
“Hehehehe.”
“Yeah, let’s.”
She gets up, and offers a hand to him.
He accepts her offer, taking her hand and lifting himself to his feet. Pocketing the parchment he'd been writing on, he steps outside.
((End session))
Alonsa follows after.

There appears to be something of a commotion outside. Civilians flee past the inn, a terrified look in their eyes. They seem to be running away from the town square.

"What the hell is going on here...?" Tanner watches the crowd.
Alonsa walks over to the town square, to see what the fuss is about.

Tanner walks beside her. As they approach the town square, the source of the commotion becomes clear. Two platoons of soldiers have gathered, weapons at the ready as their commanding officers stare one another down.
"Who are these people?"
"Soldiers from... Muk and Kham. This could be bad. My..." He holds his head. "...'memories' tell me wars in this time are rather brutal. It might be best to flee, as well."
"The one-syllable names are bothering me. Do you think with each era they add more syllables?"
"Let's keep a distance, but I want to see what happens."

"Right." Tanner hides around the corner of a building, peeking at the armies.

The commanding officers yell at one another in a heated argument. "You know Kham has authority over this region. Bringing an army here is a declaration of war!" "Ha! Authority? Muk discovered this town. Your pathetic excuse for a country couldn't have made it through the forest without us clearing the way." "So you're occupying a neutral territory? Sounds to me like all we're doing is liberating these people." "Please, don't try to take the moral high ground. We all know why we're here!"
Alonsa moves alonside Tanner. "It sounds like this happens a lot..."
"...Tensions have been rising, yes. I wonder if they even believe in their cause, or if their goals are just... excuses to fight."
"Well, if history has shown anything, it's that those are often indistinguishable."
Alonsa keeps watching.

"This is your last warning to back off! We're bringing the source of magic back, even if it kills us. Or better yet, y-" The Kham commanding officer stops mid sentence, just as he was reaching for his weapon. The entire army seems to freeze up, with their only movements coming from the breaths they take. Alonsa feels a chill run down her spine at the same moment. Something dangerous is approaching.
*Is this magic? Or just... some kind of greater authority...*
Alonsa watches intently.

The silence falling over the army makes the approaching footsteps sound deafening. The soldiers take a step back, as if by instinct, clearing the way for the danger. She stands tall, adorned with a sleek, efficient outfit, contrasting the ostentatious military garb of the armies. Bixbite looks from one commander to another, wearing a sadistic grin.
"Bixbite?"
"Huh... How did she get here..."

Tanner's pupils quiver in fear. "I'm... not sure she did. Alonsa... th-that's..."

"Th-the... THE DEMON KING'S GENERAL!?" The Kham commander screams out. "SOLDIERS... ATT-" Before he can finish his order, Bixbite's arm appears to turn into a blur. The next moment, she's holding his head by the hair. His body slumps over, separated from his head at the neck in a clean slice.
"Oh... Oh my god..."
If it isn't Bixbite, she's still equally as terrifying, it seems.
"Why is the Demon King's general here?"

Tanner tries to compose himself, averting his eyes from the sight. "The Demon King's army follows the scent of bloody conflict. They're like vultures, picking meat from the bones after wars break out. Some people say they're summoned by the souls of the dead."
"This 'Demon King' guy... wouldn't happen to be wearing a mask, would he?"
"...Those who witness him and live to tell the tale typically describe him as such, yes."
"Figures."
"There was someone like him in our time, too."
"Good news is, he's dead, I think."

"Still, I'm not sure what this means. It seems like... it might be that the whole world's been remixed into this weird alternate history. I think that might actually be Bixbite, but transported back in time with us."
"Maybe everyone here got transported back too. Actually, I doubt that."

"Maybe we should... um... ask her?" Tanner looks over to Bixbite, who's currently holding the commander's head above her, opening her mouth for the blood rushing out of the stump that used to be a neck. She licks her lips as it dries up, and tosses the head to the side.

Tanner turns back to Alonsa. "Or we could run very far away."
"We should probably get out of here before she comes after us."
"Lets go."
Alonsa runs off.

As Alonsa runs, her path is suddenly blocked by the appearance of a familiar figure. Sir Roost has come back into town, and speaks to her in a booming voice. "Ah! Alonsa, how strange that we would run into one another once again! What are you doing, over here? Behind the corner of this house? Are you hiding from something? Fleeing from it? Over here? Around this corner of the town square?"
"There's a scary lady over there who ripped a guy's head off."
"I figured we should skedaddle."

He reaches for his sword. "Such savagery! Do not fear, I will smite down evil wherever it appears! For that is my solemn vow!"

"Savage? You don't have much fun, do you?" Bixbite's cold voice rings out from right behind Alonsa. She must have been drawn here by Sir Roost's yelling.
"So loud..."
Alonsa turns around.
"Hello, Miss Bixbi- I mean, Hello, ma'am!"
She raises an eyebrow. "You know my name? How'd you get ahold of that one?" She narrows her eyes. "You know me or something?"
"Oh, no, uh..."
"I just... Have happened to meet someone who looks a lot like you... who also coincidentally shared your name..."
"Unless you... remember me? I'm Alonsa?"
She says the last part very questioningly

Her hand moves quickly, catching Sir Roost's blade as he attempts to cut her down, while she looks over Alonsa. "It's not ringing a bell, but that doesn't mean I haven't met you. I just don't really care about most humans. No point remembering them. Are you one of the army guys? I'm only supposed to kill them."
"Nope! Just a traveler!"
She says, very nervously.
"He is too, actually."
"Say, I'm not from around here. Most humans? I know you're part of the demon kingdom, or whatever, but I didn't know you guys were like... actual demons. That's cool!"

"Hi." Tanner nervously waves his hand. "Me. I'm traveler. No threat here."

Bixbite smirks at Alonsa's words. "Not... all of us. The monolithic name's just a branding thing. It's pretty varied. Plenty of humans in the demon army. Doesn't make much sense, does it?" As she explains, Sir Roost lets go of his broken sword, and begins swinging his fists ineffectively at Bixbite, not managing to move her an inch. She looks down at him. "Do you mind?"
"It is a little confusing..."
"Still, I think it's very interesting."
"So, I guess, just..." Alonsa is trying desperatly to maintain conversation. "What brings you to this town?"

"Just making preparations for the Demon King's arrival. He wants to be here when the armies get here." She motions behind her. "Those guys are just the scouts."

Sir Roost backs off, exhausted. "When... when my party of adventurers gets here... you will regret your crimes, Demon General!"
"His... armies?"
"What's gonna happen here? Just... thought I should ask to know if I should stay in this area..."

"Not sure. My king always keeps this stuff close to his chest." She reaches into her pocket, and pulls out a familiar key. "I should get back to it. I'm supposed to hide this in a fountain, for some reason?"
Alonsa looks at it in shock.
She then checks her pockets, where she left hers.
Alonsa has two keys in her pockets, neither of which match the key Bixbite is holding. As she checks, Bixbite wanders back to the town square, and Tanner breathes a sigh of relief.
"That went well!"
"That key is bothering me, though."
Tanner shakes his head. "Yeah. Who hides a key in a fountain? People would be sure to find it while fishing for change."
"Obviously, we're going to go get it, as soon as she leaves."

Sir Roost appears conflicted. "Normally, I would not condone such blatant thievery. These are desperate times, though. If it is an important task assigned by the Demon King, that key must be invaluable to his defeat."

There's some screams from the town square. Sounds like Bixbite's getting back to work at taking down the armies of Kham and Muk. Tanner mutters to himself. "You'd think they would've cleared out with all that time you bought them..."
"They should try talking to her. She's pretty nice!"
"Though, I guess I'm not in their position."
"We should look for the others while we wait for her to clear out."
"I concur. I am sure that Sneevs will find a way to neutralize that demon's strength!" Sir Roost clenches his fists with resolve.
"That's right, I never got to tell you, Sir Roost."
"We're actually... if you would believe it, from way, way, way in the future."
"Neither of us have any idea how we got here, all we know is that when we woke up, it was suddenly... whatever year it is."

Roost rubs his chin. "How peculiar! It would explain your unfamiliarity with current affairs, and your odd attire. Normally I would find it difficult to believe, but I have witnessed stranger sights on my journey, and you have an air of... how shall I say, trustworthiness about you."
*I trust him, because of his resemblence to the casts. Maybe that goes both ways?*
*But he'd have no way of knowing about them...*
"Thank you, thank you. I do my best."
"Do you know where we could find... other people, who seem to be lost, like us?"
"I am afraid I do not have confidence I am aware of such a location. Perhaps the local authorities? If I were lost, that is where I would turn!"
"Well, uhhh...."
Alonsa turns to look at the soldiers behind her, and then turns back around.
"I don't know if they'll be... consultable."
"They're a bit preoccupied."

"You misunderstand. Those foul invading armies are foreign to this land. The local knights are stationed elsewhere, and have foolishly decided to remain neutral Muk and Kham's colonization of their land. There is a garrison on the eastern end of the town."
"Ohh, alright."
"Can you take me there?"

Sir Roost shakes his head. "I am afraid not. I shall not abandon a fight. I will remain here until my party arrives."

Tanner speaks up. "It's... fine. I 'remember' where it is."
"Alright. Good luck with your... fight."
"Good tidings to you as well! Until we meet again, Alonsa." He gives her a hearty wave, and Tanner leads the way to the garrison.
((End session))
